segmentation.text: shall not stop, stand or park a vehicle,
except when necessary to avoid conflict
or the directions of a police officer
in any of the following places:
At any place where official traffic-control devices prohibit stopping, standing or parking.

elements.justification: The words name the person who stops, stands or parks "a vehicle". Who controls a vehicle is not observable; the ontology reads the one who drives through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the road user judged is the vehicle (agency reading, disclosed). ru.aggregate is "membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id"; the admitted id DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle counts "every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway", its exceptions classified by the run's reading. Not a stand-in for a named class with its own atom (the words name none), nor for the relational role of who controls the vehicle: the atom states the class of the road user whose halts are judged.

"stop" when prohibited is "any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not" (DEF-NRS-484A-260); "stand" is "the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not" other than while receiving or discharging passengers (DEF-NRS-484A-250); "park" is "the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not" (DEF-NRS-484A-155). Each is a halting; drv.motion.complete_halt denotes that "The road user is at rest at the observation", observed as kin.speed at or below a tolerance, at each observation; what it does not denote ("a slowing whose sampled speed stays above the tolerance") is no halting. Which of the three halts is forbidden at a place is the one the device there prohibits (next span). "a vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway").

"traffic" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ("pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel"); "other" leaves out the subject itself. rel.ahead_behind_in_lane ("a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction") places that traffic in the subject's path, and rel.surface_gap ("distance between the nearest points of two bodies") is the clearance to it that the operationalization of "necessary" bounds. Neither contract carries a not-a-stand-in clause this use touches; no centre distance and no order of arrival is read.

"in compliance with law" excuses a halt the law itself requires of the vehicle where it is. Observably those are the halt a stop sign requires (dev.stop_sign: "regulatory sign requiring a full halt") and the halt a traffic signal requires while it shows a red indication (dev.traffic_signal: "a signal head" with states circular_red, red_arrow(dir) and flashing_red), each on the traffic of a travel region the device governs (dev.governs: "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls") that the vehicle's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies: "a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region"; st.travel_region is the kind that relation ranges over here). dev.governs is "Not a stand-in for: a position — the region a device governs is not where a halt is required": the governed region is not read as the place of a required halt; it reads only that a vehicle within the governed approach, while the device commands a halt, is held there in obedience to it.

dev.human_direction is "a person directing traffic and the direction given; role ∈ {police_officer, flagger, school_crossing_guard, railroad_flagger}; indication ∈ {stop, proceed, slow, turn(dir)}". A police officer ("every officer authorized to direct or regulate traffic", DEF-NRS-484A-180) is the role police_officer, and the direction a halt complies with is the indication stop, given to the travel region the vehicle's footprint overlaps (dev.governs: "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls"; rel.occupies; st.travel_region the kind). dev.governs is not read as the place a halt is required, only as the traffic the direction is given to. A flagger or a crossing guard is another role and is not read.

An official traffic-control device is "every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority or railroad for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic" (DEF-NRS-484A-145). The devices whose directions a halt obeys are a stop sign (dev.stop_sign: "regulatory sign requiring a full halt"), a yield sign (dev.yield_sign: "regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt", whose yield may require a halt), a traffic signal showing circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red (dev.traffic_signal), and a level-crossing signal with its lights flashing or its gate lowering or down (dev.railway_signal_or_gate: "lights ∈ {flashing, dark}; gate ∈ {up, lowering, down, raising, none}"), each governing the travel region the vehicle occupies (dev.governs, rel.occupies, st.travel_region). "official" is the device's legal status, read from its presence. dev.governs is not read as the position of a required halt, only as the traffic the device directs; no sign is read as a manoeuvre.

An official traffic-control device is "every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority or railroad for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic" (DEF-NRS-484A-145). The devices that prohibit stopping, standing or parking are the point regulations dev.regulatory_sign of code no_stopping, no_standing or no_parking ("a point regulation by catalogue code"), in effect for the vehicle where their stated conditions hold at the observation (prim.conditions_hold: "the structured conditions of a device ... hold at the observation for a road user"), governing a travel region the vehicle's footprint overlaps (dev.governs, rel.occupies, st.travel_region); and the marked or signed lengths of curb st.curb_zone of kind no_stopping or no_parking ("a signed or marked length of curb") that the vehicle's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies). Each prohibition reads the halt it names: "stopping" when prohibited is "any halting, even momentarily" (DEF-NRS-484A-260), drv.motion.complete_halt; "standing" is "the halting of a vehicle" otherwise than while receiving or discharging passengers (DEF-NRS-484A-250) and "parking" "the standing of a vehicle" otherwise than temporarily while loading or unloading (DEF-NRS-484A-155), each read through how long the vehicle has been at rest, drv.motion.parked ("at rest at every observation of the window behind the observation, of length min_duration"), with p.standing_min_duration and p.parking_min_duration. dev.regulatory_sign is "Not a stand-in for: a manoeuvre or a road feature — a prohibition sign is a condition": it is read as exactly that condition. dev.governs is read as the traffic the sign regulates, not as a halt position.

operationalizations.standard: necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic
operationalizations.convention: queue spacing of halted vehicles: a halt with a member of traffic ahead in the same lane within that gap between bodies is a halt the traffic ahead makes necessary

applicability: The subject is a road user of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, and at the observation either a dev.regulatory_sign of code no_stopping, no_standing or no_parking whose conditions hold for the subject (prim.conditions_hold) governs (dev.governs) a travel region whose footprint the subject's overlaps (rel.occupies), or the subject's footprint overlaps a st.curb_zone of kind no_stopping or no_parking.
obligation: At every observation at which the applicability holds, the subject is not engaged in the conduct a device there prohibits: where a no_stopping sign or curb zone applies, the subject is not at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance); where a no_standing sign applies, it is not standing (drv.motion.parked with p.halt_speed_tolerance and p.standing_min_duration); where a no_parking sign or curb zone applies, it is not parked (drv.motion.parked with p.halt_speed_tolerance and p.parking_min_duration); unless at that observation one of the exceptions holds: (a) some road user other than the subject, of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, is ahead of the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with the gap between their bodies (rel.surface_gap) at most p.queue_halt_gap; (b) a stop sign, or a traffic signal showing circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red, governs (dev.governs) a travel region the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies); (c) a dev.human_direction of role police_officer with indication stop governs a travel region the subject occupies; (d) a stop sign, a yield sign, a traffic signal showing circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red, or a dev.railway_signal_or_gate with lights flashing or gate lowering or down governs a travel region the subject occupies. Violated where the subject engages in a prohibited halt there and no exception holds.

narrowings.why: The person who stops the vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the rule judges the vehicle's halts whoever or whatever controls it.

"necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic" is read only as a halt with a member of traffic ahead in the same lane within the queue gap; a halt to let crossing or oncoming traffic clear, with nothing ahead in the lane, is not read as necessary, so such a halt is judged without this exception.
"official" is the device's legal status, read from the device's presence in the scene.
"official" said of the prohibiting devices is their legal status, read from the sign's or the marked curb's presence in the scene.

Standing and parking are told from a halt by their purpose (receiving or discharging passengers, temporary loading or unloading), which is not observable; the purpose is read through how long the vehicle has been at rest.

The prohibition is read respectively to the place: where a device prohibits stopping, any halt is forbidden; where it prohibits standing, standing; where it prohibits parking, parking. A brief halt where a device prohibits only parking is not read as forbidden, since the device there permits it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A dev.regulatory_sign of code no_parking with empty conditions governs the lane the subject, a ru.aggregate vehicle, occupies; the subject has been at rest (kin.speed zero) for 300 s; no other road user, no human direction and no other device is in the scene.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the subject has been at rest for 20 s after moving, a halt shorter than parking.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject is at rest in a lane that no prohibiting sign governs and overlaps no curb zone.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not observe the subject's speed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A dev.regulatory_sign of code no_stopping with empty conditions governs the subject's lane; the subject halts for 2 s.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The subject's footprint overlaps a st.curb_zone of kind no_parking and it has been at rest for 400 s.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the sign's conditions state a time window that env.civil_time at the observation lies outside, so prim.conditions_hold is false.

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: As in branch_1, but another vehicle stands ahead of the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with its body 2 m from the subject's (rel.surface_gap).

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition source's kinematics

param_proposals.name: p.queue_halt_gap
param_proposals.convention: the gap between bodies to a road user ahead in the same lane within which a halt is a halt behind other traffic: the spacing of halted vehicles in a queue
param_proposals.source: jam spacing of halted vehicles in traffic-flow studies (Highway Capacity Manual)

param_proposals.name: p.standing_min_duration
param_proposals.convention: the longest halt counted as receiving or discharging passengers or loading rather than standing: a passenger pick-up dwell at the curb
param_proposals.source: curbside passenger pick-up dwell times in curb-management studies

param_proposals.name: p.parking_min_duration
param_proposals.convention: the longest halt counted as temporary, as for loading or unloading: a common time limit of a passenger loading zone
param_proposals.source: municipal passenger loading zone time limits
